source.title: Lumbar MRI
source.note: Criteria text below is drawn from the public CMS Local Coverage Determination. Used verbatim where quoted so the prototype checks against real Medicare coverage language, not invented rules.

criteria.text: Lumbar MRI is covered for patients with red-flag conditions suggesting medical urgency, including suspected tumor, infection, herniated disc with nerve compression, or major neurological problems.
redFlags: major trauma, or minor trauma in a patient with osteoporosis
fever, chills, or unexplained weight loss
bacterial infection or IV drug use
anal sphincter laxity or perianal sensory loss
criteria.effect: If any red flag is present and documented, imaging is permitted without delay and the conservative management requirement does not apply.

criteria.text: MRI will be covered only if the patient has not responded to a reasonable trial of conservative management lasting at least four weeks.
evidenceAccepted: physical therapy course with dates and outcome
documented trial of NSAIDs or other analgesics with dates
chiropractic care with dates and outcome
home exercise program with documented adherence and duration
criteria.commonFailure: Conservative management is frequently documented in outside records, prior-practice notes, or therapy discharge summaries rather than in the referring physician's note attached to the request.

criteria.text: Duplication of other imaging studies is not covered absent inconclusive CT findings or a documented change in clinical status.
criteria.effect: A repeat lumbar MRI without documented interval change in symptoms or findings does not meet coverage criteria.

criteria.text: Uncomplicated degenerative disc disease without surgical consideration is not covered.
criteria.effect: Imaging solely to characterize known DDD, where no surgical or interventional decision depends on the result, does not meet coverage criteria.

criteria.text: Lumbar MRI abnormalities alone do not validate the need for the test without other supporting clinical rationale. Medical records must demonstrate that the service is reasonable and necessary, and an attending physician order is required.
